candidate_findings.title: Sliding-window scans lack a coherent watermark and atomic publication contract
candidate_findings.claim: The scan may use a time window or an incremental checkpoint, may persist either a sequence or timestamp checkpoint, and may be launched periodically or on demand, but this span does not define event-time semantics, late events, window eviction, overlapping-run exclusion, or atomic rollup-plus-checkpoint publication.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An incremental scan can retain samples that have aged out, while overlap or a crash can expose a checkpoint from one generation with partial rollups from another; every dashboard consumer then displays the corrupted generation.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Choose one canonical sequence watermark tied to an explicit event-time cutoff; define late and clock-skew handling, expiry/rebuild behavior, a lease or generation CAS for overlapping scans, atomic publication of all rollups with their checkpoint, crash recovery, and deterministic crash/overlap fixtures.

candidate_findings.missing_contract: Specify the exact 24h inputs, aggregation keys, metadata key, publication behavior, consumer fallback, and a test asserting all canonical windows are produced together.

candidate_findings.title: Analytics metric definitions permit incompatible results
candidate_findings.claim: The compute contract permits summing tokens or request count and does not define the platform dimension, run-failure denominator, zero-sample behavior, percentile algorithm, missing latency handling, or deduplication between usage and completion events.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two conforming projectors can publish materially different values under identical input, so no stable test oracle or cross-version comparison exists.

candidate_findings.title: Worktree rename events are omitted from binding-projection replay
candidate_findings.claim: The disposable worktree-binding projections are rebuilt only from bound and unbound events even though the binding payload contains a branch name and rename is a registered lifecycle event.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: After rebuild, the thread binding can regress to the old branch name, causing stale GUI truth, audit joins, or subsequent routing to disagree with the worktree record.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Require rename events in the projector, define behavior for rename-before-bind, duplicate and missing-old-name cases, update both forward and reverse records atomically, and add live-versus-rebuild equivalence tests.

candidate_findings.title: Missing worktree attribution silently becomes main-project context
candidate_findings.claim: A background event from a bound thread may omit both worktree fields, and consumers are instructed to interpret that omission as main-project context; omission is therefore indistinguishable from an intentional main-project dispatch.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A producer bug, schema downgrade, or partial event can route mutation-capable background work into the main checkout rather than the isolated worktree.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Persist a required `execution_context` discriminator and stable `worktree_id`; reject or quarantine absent attribution when the thread is bound; reserve an explicit legacy-main sentinel for migrated events; verify context against the safe-point snapshot before dispatch.

candidate_findings.title: Worktree side-effect events lack attempt identity and precondition data
candidate_findings.claim: Merge, PR, and pre-merge-test payloads have no operation or attempt ID, idempotency key, causation reference, or pre-operation source/target SHAs; the stated envelope supplies only timestamp, sequence, type, and payload.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Parallel identical tests cannot be paired reliably with passed or failed events, and retries after uncertain push, PR, or merge outcomes can duplicate side effects or attach a result to the wrong operation.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Add stable event and operation IDs, attempt number, causation/start reference, idempotency key, actor, source and target precondition SHAs, command hash, remote request/object identifiers, and retry-reconciliation tests.

candidate_findings.title: Runtime checkpoint markers have no crash-point semantics
candidate_findings.claim: Markers are required before resume or restore continues, but this span gives no marker schema or planned, started, committed, aborted, or consumed transition that links the marker to the external mutation.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A crash after marker durability but before mutation, or after mutation but before the next marker, is not deterministically distinguishable; replay can skip required work or duplicate a mutation.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define recovery-attempt identity, safe-point hash and lineage, operation idempotency key, explicit intent/start/commit/abort states, durability acknowledgements, reconciliation rules for every crash boundary, and crash-injection oracles.

candidate_findings.title: Overlapping runtime identity fields lack an authoritative mapping
candidate_findings.claim: The shared identity table introduces `requested_account_binding` and `effective_provider_identity`, while the required list separately introduces `requested_account_id`, `effective_account_id`, and `account_id`; types, nullability, cardinality, relationships, and precedence are not stated.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Permission checks, usage attribution, history, and GUI labels can select different account identities for the same frozen attempt, weakening audit integrity and no-silent-fallback guarantees.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Provide one versioned typed snapshot schema, exact mappings and invariants among binding, provider identity, effective account and account ID, behavior for anonymous or unresolved accounts, credential-reference constraints, and conflict rejection rules.

candidate_findings.title: Questionnaire persistence defines two unmapped status domains
candidate_findings.claim: One list is declared the canonical status set while a second list supplies draft, readiness, submitted, and paused flow states, including both `draft` and `/draft`, without assigning them to item versus questionnaire fields or defining transitions.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Reload, timeout, resend, and multi-question submission can restore contradictory states or submit an answer twice because `submitted` and draft lifecycle meanings are not scoped.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define separate item and session status fields, remove or normalize `/draft`, specify transition authority and allowed edges, deadlines and timeout races, send/resend idempotency, terminal invariants, and state-machine fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: The minimal TODO mutation event cannot replay structural revisions atomically
candidate_findings.claim: The contract requires create, reorder, structural revision, and plan supersession behavior, but the event carries one `todo_id`, one untyped field change, and no event ID, base revision, new revision, or batch boundary.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A multi-item reorder or Deep Plan resync can be partially visible after a crash, concurrent user and agent changes can overwrite one another, and replay cannot prove which normalized list corresponds to the approved plan panel.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define typed create, remove, update, reorder and plan-level operations; event and revision IDs; base/new revision CAS; ordered batch semantics or a complete order snapshot; system/heuristic source handling; idempotency; conflict policy; and deterministic replay tests.

candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a progress-event schema carrying attempt ID and progress sequence, allowed phases and transitions, monotonic completed/total invariants, heartbeat timeout, terminal precedence, partial-result finality, duplicate handling, and adversarial ordering tests.

candidate_findings.title: Sensitive command and web-input persistence has no bounded storage-hygiene contract
candidate_findings.claim: The span requires durable raw command blocks plus web input previews, URLs, browser session identifiers, source references, and error data, but states no redaction, encryption, reader authorization, inline-field retention, deletion, or export-scrubbing rules for them.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Commands and browsing inputs commonly contain tokens, credentials, private paths, query text, and sensitive URLs that can leak through history, audit, backups, or exports indefinitely.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Classify sensitive fields; scrub secrets before append; encrypt at rest with key-rotation rules; authorize readers by project and actor; define inline and referenced retention, deletion and legal-hold behavior; sanitize exports and diagnostics; and test known secret patterns.

candidate_findings.title: Persisted executable visualizers are re-run without policy-version or revocation semantics
candidate_findings.claim: HTML, JavaScript, CSS, and third-party script references are persisted and re-rendered on reload or export; pinning, integrity and policy approval are required when recorded, but the span does not persist the sandbox or policy version or say what happens when approval is revoked, a dependency disappears, or runtime compatibility changes.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Previously accepted code can become unsafe or behave differently under a later runtime, creating stored-script execution risk and non-reproducible history or exports.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Persist runtime, sandbox and policy versions; define CSP, origin, network and bridge capabilities; revalidate on every execution; quarantine revoked or unverifiable modules; disclose stale screenshot fallback; define dependency-unavailable behavior and compatibility test vectors.

candidate_findings.title: The editor recovery implementation omits recoverable buffer bytes and required identity
candidate_findings.claim: Recovery rules require local buffer state, capture metadata, host/path identity, and write availability, but the implementation lists only cursor, scroll, selection, an undo-stack reference, and an unsaved flag under a project-plus-path-hash key; it does not explicitly persist unsaved content, a delta, base revision, capture metadata, host identity, or write availability.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: After a crash the system may know that edits existed without being able to restore or diff them, and local and remote files with the same path identity can collide or restore into the wrong destination.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Persist content or a durable delta/blob reference, base content hash and destination revision, capture sequence/time, host identity in the key derivation, write-availability snapshot, collision handling, atomic capture cadence, size limits, cleanup after resolution, and crash/conflict oracles.

candidate_findings.title: Requested and effective state can tear across keys, while health remains underspecified
candidate_findings.claim: Requested and effective values use separate keys without a shared resolution generation or transactional-read rule. The required distinctions include freshness, health, and write availability, but the implementation defines only freshness values, while the adjacent LSP context also requires degraded and unavailable disclosure.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: A crash or concurrent re-resolution can pair a new requested state with an old effective state and still label it current, causing the GUI and history to misrepresent actual capabilities or remote write safety.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Add a shared resolution ID, schema version and timestamps; atomically publish or coherently read both keys; define health and write-availability enums separately from freshness; specify transition and stale-age rules, crash fallback, and cross-key consistency tests.

candidate_findings.title: Project-only Source Control state cannot isolate concurrent worktrees
candidate_findings.claim: Worktree state is explicitly project-and-worktree scoped, but Source Control uses one project-only key for branch, staged files, commit draft, compare targets, review notes, and conflict preferences.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Two worktrees in one project can overwrite each other's staged projection, commit message, branch, compare target, and review context, potentially leading the user to inspect or commit the wrong checkout.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Scope repository state by host, repository and worktree identity; distinguish project preferences from worktree state; validate the active binding on every mutation; define branch-change, removal and migration invalidation; and test two simultaneous worktrees.

candidate_findings.title: Stale compare-target retention is not testable
candidate_findings.claim: The requirement retains stale targets only 'long enough' without a duration, event-driven deletion condition, owner, or behavior when the replacement also becomes stale.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Implementations can retain obsolete branch and review references indefinitely or delete them before the downgrade explanation is visible, producing divergent recovery UX and unbounded stale state.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define a TTL or acknowledged-downgrade transition, the responsible projector, replacement chaining, deletion and legal-hold interaction, consumer behavior after expiry, and a clock-independent test oracle.

candidate_findings.title: Persisted Search results have no bound, indirection, or invalidation generation
candidate_findings.claim: The Search projection is specified to store results directly but has no maximum count or bytes, pagination/blob rule, index generation, query snapshot identifier, TTL, or invalidation rule after repository changes.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: Large searches can bloat redb and restarts can present old results as current after files, filters, or the underlying index changed.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define result caps and paging, inline-versus-reference threshold, query hash and index generation, freshness state, repository-change invalidation, eviction and retention, and scale fixtures.

candidate_findings.title: GitHub correlation confidence lacks deterministic semantics
candidate_findings.claim: The project state stores a confidence threshold plus auto-open hints and related-worktree preference, but no confidence domain, default, producer/algorithm version, calibration oracle, or rule preventing automatic navigation from weak or stale candidates is supplied.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: The same evidence can select different files or worktrees across implementations or versions, making heuristic evidence appear operationally authoritative despite the noncanonical warning.
candidate_findings.missing_contract: Define score range and meaning, default and ownership, algorithm/version persistence, evidence freshness, minimum threshold for hints versus auto-open, confirmation requirements for context-changing actions, and calibrated fixtures.
